messages:
maria: FYI customer-trust asked for an air-gapped deployment checklist + evidence for KMS/HSM integration and RBAC separation. They want: key custody proof, audit log export path, and vuln triage timeline. Meeting set for 15:00 PT to align.
aj: Do we have an approved pattern for on-prem KMS envelope wrapping? specifically they asked about customer-managed keys vs hardware module in their datacenter.
kevin: We usually support both via our private deployment: option A = customer KMS with envelope keys (we never hold plaintext), option B = HSM appliance + attestation report. For A we need docs showing key lifecycle and access controls.
eva: Also they want SIEM ingestion for audit logs with guaranteed ordering and tamper-evidence. Current private build supports syslog/HTTPS forwarders. Need to confirm retention and signing.
maria: Good point. @kevin can you paste the minimal RBAC policy we recommend for operators vs auditors? we should include an example in the evidence bundle.
kevin: Sure. Minimal example (placeholder):
```
- role: inference_operator
  permissions: [deploy:create, runtime:start, runtime:stop]
- role: auditor
  permissions: [audit:read, logs:export]
```
kevin: Note: operators do NOT get audit:read by default; auditors are scoped to read-only with denylists for PII.
aj: On key proofs — we can provide KMS access logs showing key use with nonce, and an attestation PDF from our HSM partner for on-prem installs. Security needs to redact tenant IDs in exported logs unless customer explicitly requests.
sec-bot: Runbook updated: https://internal.redwood.dev/runbooks/private-deploy-kms-checklist — last edited by sec-bot at 2023-10-12.
maria: Action items: 1) kevin draft RBAC policy + example claims (owner: kevin) 2) aj collect KMS usage samples and attestation artifacts (owner: aj) 3) eva confirm SIEM pipeline and retention limits (owner: eva) 4) I will assemble an evidence README and a redaction checklist (owner: maria).
eva: For SIEM: we support TLS+mutual auth + signed batches. Retention is configurable per customer; default 90d. For tamper-evidence we'll sign batches with rotating service keys — include the signing key rotation cadence in the docs.
aj: Vulnerability triage note: if the customer runs a pen-test and finds a vuln in runtime, our SLA for triage is 48h initial response, full triage in 5 business days. Need to include process and contact points in the package.
maria: Can someone grab the last customer-facing evidence bundle we shipped (ver 2023-09) and attach it here before the call? I want to avoid re-creating artifacts.
kevin: Pulling it now from /s3/private-evidence/bundles/2023-09. I can sanitize tenant IDs and drop raw logs.
sec-bot: Evidence template created: /templates/evidence-airgap-kms.md
maria: If we need a demo of key wrap, we can run a short local demo during the call: show envelope encryption flow + logs to SIEM. 10m demo slot ok?
aj: Works for me. Also add a snippet showing how we rotate ephemeral service accounts after an incident — customers ask about forensics and short-lived creds.
kevin: Snippet for ephemeral account creation (k8s service-account + TTL controller):
```
kubectl create serviceaccount rw-ephemeral --namespace=prod
# TTL controller will auto-expire after 1h
```
maria: Great. I'll update the runbook with a section "evidence redaction checklist" and ping compliance for signoff. Meeting in 30.
eva: I'll confirm SIEM endpoints and test a signed batch before the call.
aj: I'll bring the KMS access log sample and a sanitized attestation report.
maria: Thanks — see you in the meeting. If anything blocks, DM me. :white_check_mark:
